content.title: About
content.content: Honey butter is a creamy spread made by blending natural honey with butter. It combines the sweetness of honey with a smooth buttery texture, making it a versatile ingredient for breakfasts, baking, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tradition of mixing honey and butter is popular in Scandinavian countries, where the spread is often served with rolls and bread.
Butter helps stabilize honey, preventing crystallization.
Honey butter can be flavored with cinnamon, vanilla, nuts, or other additions.
When stored properly, the product can keep its quality for up to a year.
The honey‑butter combination enhances flavor perception, making sweetness feel softer.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Honey contains flavonoids and phenolic compounds that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: Simple sugars in honey are quickly absorbed, providing a rapid source of energy.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Honey provides B2, B3, and B5 vitamins, important for metabolism.

items.title: Healthy fats
items.content: Butter contributes monounsaturated fats that can support heart health when consumed in moderation.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Honey has mild prebiotic effects, promoting the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Allergy to honey or dairy
items.content: People allergic to pollen, honey, or milk proteins may experience reactions.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Honey is rich in simple sugars, so individuals with diabetes should limit intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Butter adds significant calories, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Infant botulism risk
items.content: Honey should not be given to children under one year due to the risk of botulism.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Spread honey butter on toast, pancakes, waffles, stir into oatmeal, yogurt, smoothies, or use it as a filling for baked goods and cookies.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight jar in the refrigerator. At room temperature the spread may soften but remains tasty for 2–3 weeks.
